name: Contact Picker
plain: Lets a person choose contacts to share with a site; Chrome on Android only.
meaning: The site gets only the names, emails, phones, addresses or icons of the contacts the person ticks. No bulk read, no desktop, no Firefox, no Safari release.

access.prompt_ui: Native Android contact chooser with search; shows which fields the page asks for
access.persistence: None; each call opens the picker again
access.iframe: Top level frame only; blocked in cross-origin iframes

data.metric: Lets a person choose contacts to share with a site; Chrome on Android only.

fields.name: name
fields.precision: as stored in the address book

fields.name: email
fields.precision: every address of each picked contact

fields.name: address
fields.precision: country, city, postalCode, region, addressLine, recipient, organization, phone

limits.headline: Can see only the contacts you pick, and only the details it asks for
limits.user_action: You tap Choose contacts, search and select people, and press Done.
can: Show a list of your contacts that you can search
Share the names, emails or phone numbers you pick
Share only the kinds of details the page asks for, shown before you choose
cannot: See contacts you did not pick
Work on desktop browsers, where it is not offered
Keep access after you pick, so it asks again each time
limits.differs: Only Chrome on Android fully supports it. iPhone Safari has it behind a setting. Desktop browsers do not.

story.what_it_is: A site can ask you to pick contacts to share, on Chrome for Android.

marketing.name: Contact Picker API
marketing.pitch: Chrome's docs say the API lets users share chosen contacts with a web app.

story.for_you: A list of your contacts opens. You tick the people to share and the site gets only those names, emails or numbers.
story.for_makers: Makers can add 'invite friends' and 'send to a contact' without asking for your whole address book. It cuts growth friction and stays safer than bulk access.

use_cases.example: A web app lets you invite friends by picking them from your contacts.
A web payment page lets you pick the person you want to pay.
A web chat app suggests who to message.
A browser game lets you pick friends to invite to a match.
A gift site picks the recipient's address from your contacts.
A scam site could repeat the picker to collect many contacts.

technical_bounds: Only picked contacts, never the whole book
Chrome Android only; not desktop Chrome or Edge, Firefox, desktop Safari
Safari iOS behind a developer flag
Needs HTTPS and a user tap; top level frame only
getProperties() reports which fields exist, not the data

history.change: Contact Picker ships on Chrome Android only
iOS exposes it only behind a preference flag; never shipped by default
Samsung exposed but contact selector failed; removed in 22
